text: Billing Policy
Customers are responsible for reviewing their billing details and monthly charges.
If a customer notices an incorrect charge, unexpected charge, duplicate charge, or charge for a service they did not expect, the billing issue should be reviewed by customer support.
Customers should provide the relevant customer, order, invoice, or transaction information when reporting a billing problem.
If a payment was successful but the order was not confirmed, the payment status and order status should be checked before another payment is attempted.
Customers should not make a second payment until the status of the original transaction has been verified.
If a customer is charged twice for the same purchase, the duplicate transaction should be reviewed by the billing support team.
If the billed amount differs from the expected amount, the applicable invoice and transaction details should be verified.
Billing records should be checked before confirming that a charge is incorrect.
The assistant must not invent transaction amounts, invoice details, payment status, or billing adjustments.
A billing investigation does not automatically result in a refund or account adjustment.
If the available information is insufficient to verify a billing issue, human customer support may be required.
Customers should not provide unnecessary sensitive payment information when requesting billing assistance.
Billing-related cases that cannot be verified from available records should be escalated to the billing support team.
Cancellation Policy
Customers may request cancellation of an order before the order reaches a stage where cancellation is no longer possible.
Cancellation requests should be checked against the current order status.
If an order is still eligible for cancellation, the support process can proceed with the cancellation request.
If the order has already entered a non-cancellable stage, cancellation may not be available.
Customers should provide the relevant order information when requesting cancellation.
A cancellation request does not guarantee that an order can be cancelled.
The assistant must not claim that an order has been cancelled unless the cancellation has been confirmed in the customer records.
If an order cannot be cancelled, other applicable options should be reviewed by customer support.
If payment has already been processed, the payment and cancellation status should be verified before discussing a possible refund.
The assistant must not invent cancellation deadlines or order statuses.
If the available information does not show whether an order can be cancelled, human customer support should review the order.
Cancellation eligibility and refund eligibility are separate decisions and should not be treated as automatically equivalent.
Customers should provide accurate order information so that the current order status can be verified.
Customer Service Guidelines
Customer support responses should be professional, concise, clear, and relevant to the customer's question.
Support responses must use only verified information available in customer records and the approved knowledge base.
The assistant must not invent product specifications, policies, order information, payment information, delivery information, or troubleshooting procedures.
When the available information is insufficient, the assistant should clearly state that additional information or human customer support is required.
The assistant should not request unnecessary personal information.
For account-specific questions, customer information should be retrieved through the appropriate customer profile tool.
For churn-related questions, the churn prediction tool should be used.
For questions asking why a customer is at risk, the SHAP explanation tool should be used to identify the main factors affecting the prediction.
For general support, billing, refund, cancellation, delivery, warranty, and technical questions, the business knowledge base should be searched before generating an answer.
The assistant should provide grounded answers and avoid unsupported claims.
The assistant should not reveal internal implementation details such as embeddings, vector databases, retrieval mechanisms, or model names to customers.
The assistant should not claim that an action has been completed unless the system has actually performed or verified that action.
If a question cannot be answered from available information, the assistant should recommend human support rather than inventing an answer.
Responses should focus on the customer's question and avoid unnecessary explanations.
Sensitive customer information should not be requested unless it is necessary for the requested support operation.
Delivery Policy
Customers can contact support when an order has not been received, has been delayed, or has an unexpected delivery status.
Delivery-related issues should be checked using the available order and delivery information.
If an order is delayed, the current order status should be verified before providing an estimated resolution.
If an order is marked as delivered but the customer has not received it, the delivery details should be reviewed and the issue should be escalated when necessary.
Customers should provide the relevant order information when requesting delivery assistance.
The system must not invent delivery dates, tracking information, delivery locations, or shipment status.
If an order is still in transit, the available delivery information should be checked before making claims about its arrival.
If delivery information cannot be verified, human customer support may be required.
A delayed delivery does not automatically indicate that an order has been lost.
A delivered status does not automatically confirm that the customer personally received the order.
If an order appears to have been delivered incorrectly, the delivery information should be reviewed by customer support.
The assistant must not guarantee a delivery date unless that information is available in verified customer records.
Customers should provide accurate order information so that delivery status can be checked.
Delivery issues involving missing, damaged, or incorrectly delivered products may require additional investigation.
Customer Support Escalation Policy
Customer issues should be escalated to human support when the available information is insufficient to provide a reliable answer.
Billing disputes involving incorrect charges, duplicate charges, or transactions that cannot be verified should be reviewed by the billing support team.
Refund requests should be escalated when refund eligibility cannot be determined from the available purchase information and applicable refund conditions.
Cancellation requests should be escalated when the current order status does not show whether cancellation is still possible.
Technical issues should be escalated when documented troubleshooting steps are unavailable, unsuccessful, or inappropriate for the reported problem.
Technical issues involving possible safety concerns should not be handled through unsupported troubleshooting instructions and should be referred to appropriate human support.
Warranty requests should be escalated when product information, purchase information, warranty conditions, or eligibility cannot be verified.
Delivery issues should be escalated when an order is marked as delivered but the customer has not received it and the available delivery information cannot resolve the issue.
Account-related problems should be escalated when the available customer information is insufficient to verify or resolve the issue.
Payment problems should be escalated when the transaction status cannot be verified or when repeated payment attempts may create additional charges.
The assistant must not invent missing customer records, order information, payment information, delivery information, warranty conditions, or product specifications.
The assistant should clearly explain when additional information or human support is required.
Escalation does not guarantee approval of a refund, replacement, cancellation, warranty claim, or other requested resolution.
When an issue is escalated, the support team should receive the relevant customer information, issue description, available transaction information, and actions already attempted.
The assistant should remain concise and professional when recommending escalation.
The assistant must never claim that a case has been escalated unless an actual escalation action has been performed by the system.
If a customer asks for an action that the system cannot perform, the assistant should clearly explain the limitation and recommend the appropriate support channel.
Payment Policy
Customers should verify their payment status when a transaction does not appear to have completed correctly.
If a payment fails, the customer should verify the payment status before attempting another transaction.
If a payment appears to have been deducted but the order was not confirmed, the transaction and order status should be checked before another payment is attempted.
Customers should not make repeated payments for the same transaction until the status of the original payment has been verified.
If a customer is charged twice for the same purchase, the duplicate transaction should be reviewed by the billing support team.
If a payment is shown as successful but the related order is missing, the payment and order records should be checked.
The assistant must not claim that a payment was successful, failed, reversed, or refunded unless the status is available in verified records.
The assistant must not invent transaction IDs, payment amounts, payment dates, or processing times.
Payment-related issues may require review by the payment or billing support team.
If a payment problem cannot be verified from available information, the issue should be escalated to human customer support.
Customers should not provide unnecessary card numbers, passwords, PINs, or authentication credentials when requesting support.
Payment verification and refund processing are separate processes.
A successful payment does not automatically mean that an order has been successfully completed.
If the payment status is unclear, customers should wait for verification rather than repeatedly submitting the same payment.
Refund Policy
Customers may request a refund when an eligible purchase requires cancellation or when a product or service qualifies for a refund.
Refund requests must be reviewed against the applicable purchase and refund conditions.
Customers should provide the order or transaction information required to identify the purchase.
A refund request does not guarantee automatic approval.
The support team must verify the transaction and applicable refund conditions before confirming eligibility.
If a customer received a damaged, defective, or incorrect product, the case should be reviewed to determine whether a refund or replacement is applicable.
If a payment was completed but the purchase was not successfully processed, the transaction should be verified before a refund is promised.
If a refund has been approved, processing may require additional time depending on the payment method and applicable processing procedures.
The assistant must not guarantee a refund before eligibility has been verified.
The assistant must not invent refund amounts, processing times, or eligibility conditions that are not documented.
If the available information is insufficient to determine refund eligibility, the request should be escalated to human customer support.
Customers should retain relevant order or transaction information when requesting a refund.
A refund request and refund approval are separate processes. Submitting a request does not mean that the refund has already been approved.
Technical Support Procedure
Customers experiencing technical problems should first describe the product, the problem observed, and when the problem started.
Customers should provide relevant error messages, warning indicators, unusual behavior, or other observable symptoms when available.
If a product does not work after installation, the customer should confirm that the installation was completed correctly and describe what happens when the product is started.

If the customer has already performed a factory reset and the problem continues, the issue should be escalated for further technical investigation rather than repeatedly recommending the same reset procedure.
If a product stopped working after a software update, the issue should be reviewed to determine whether the update may be related to the problem.
Support staff should recommend only troubleshooting procedures that are documented for the particular product.
The assistant must not invent product-specific troubleshooting instructions.
Customers should not be instructed to perform repairs, hardware modifications, electrical work, or other potentially unsafe procedures.
If the available information does not contain a safe troubleshooting procedure, the customer should be referred to technical support.
If the same problem continues after documented troubleshooting steps have been completed, the issue should be escalated for further investigation.

When escalating a technical issue, the available product information, symptoms, error messages, troubleshooting steps already attempted, and relevant order information should be provided to the support team.
If a product appears to have physical damage, the case should be reviewed before additional troubleshooting is recommended.
If a customer reports a safety-related problem, the customer should stop using the product and contact appropriate human support.
Technical support should not guarantee a repair, replacement, refund, or resolution until the case has been reviewed.
The assistant should clearly state when the available information is insufficient to identify the cause of a technical problem.
Warranty Policy
Warranty-related requests must be reviewed against the applicable product warranty conditions.
Customers should provide the product information and purchase details required to verify warranty eligibility.
A product that stops working or arrives with a defect may require inspection before a replacement or warranty service is approved.
Physical damage, unauthorized modification, misuse, or other conditions may affect warranty eligibility depending on the applicable warranty terms.
If a product is defective during the applicable warranty period, the case should be reviewed by customer support.
Warranty eligibility does not automatically guarantee a replacement or repair.
The assistant must not claim that a product is covered by warranty without verifying the applicable conditions.
The assistant must not invent warranty periods, coverage conditions, exclusions, or replacement procedures.
If a product has been modified or repaired by an unauthorized party, warranty eligibility should be reviewed before any conclusion is provided.
If warranty eligibility cannot be determined from the available information, the request should be escalated to customer support.
Customers should provide relevant purchase information and product details when requesting warranty assistance.
Customers should not be asked to perform potentially unsafe repairs or modifications.
A warranty review and warranty approval are separate processes.
Warranty approval does not automatically specify whether the final resolution will be repair, replacement, or another applicable service.
